tx-10.learn: Writes and votes on federal laws; all federal tax and spending bills start in the House, which can impeach federal officials. 2-year term.

tx-37.learn: Writes and votes on federal laws; all federal tax and spending bills start in the House, which can impeach federal officials. 2-year term.

us-senate-tx.learn: Writes federal laws, approves the federal budget with the House, confirms judges, cabinet members and ambassadors, and ratifies treaties. 6-year term; Texas has 2 senators.

tx-gov.learn: Signs or vetoes bills (including line-item budget vetoes), calls special legislative sessions, appoints many state board members, and commands state military forces. 4-year term.

tx-ltgov.learn: Presides over the Texas Senate, appoints Senate committees, controls which bills reach the floor, and co-chairs the Legislative Budget Board. 4-year term.

tx-ag.learn: The state's lawyer: represents Texas in court, issues legal opinions to state officials, and runs child-support enforcement and consumer-protection divisions. 4-year term.

tx-comptroller.learn: The state's chief tax collector, accountant and revenue estimator; certifies that the state budget fits within estimated revenue and manages state funds. 4-year term.

tx-land.learn: Runs the General Land Office: state-owned land and mineral rights supporting the Permanent School Fund, the Gulf coast, the Alamo, and veterans' land programs. 4-year term.

tx-agcomm.learn: Runs the Texas Department of Agriculture: farm and ranch programs, school-lunch programs, pesticide regulation, and inspection of gas pumps and scales. 4-year term.

tx-rrc.learn: Regulates Texas oil and natural gas (drilling permits, pipelines, gas utilities) and surface coal and uranium mining, not railroads. 3 commissioners, 6-year staggered terms.

tx-supreme-court-place-1-chief-justice.learn: Highest Texas court for civil and juvenile cases; justices run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

tx-supreme-court-place-7.learn: Highest Texas court for civil and juvenile cases; justices run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

tx-supreme-court-place-8.learn: Highest Texas court for civil and juvenile cases; justices run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

tx-supreme-court-place-2.learn: Highest Texas court for civil and juvenile cases; justices run in partisan elections for 6-year terms; this seat fills the remainder of an unexpired term.

tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-3.office: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals Place 3
tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-3.learn: Highest Texas court for criminal cases, including all death-penalty appeals; judges run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-4.office: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals Place 4
tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-4.learn: Highest Texas court for criminal cases, including all death-penalty appeals; judges run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-9.office: Texas Court of Criminal Appeals Place 9
tx-court-of-criminal-appeals-place-9.learn: Highest Texas court for criminal cases, including all death-penalty appeals; judges run in partisan elections for 6-year terms.

ca-11.learn: Writes and votes on federal laws; all federal tax and spending bills start in the House, which can impeach federal officials. 2-year term.

ca-ag.learn: Chief law officer: heads the state Department of Justice, represents California in court, and oversees law enforcement statewide. 4-year term.

ca-controller.learn: Chief fiscal officer: pays state bills and payroll, audits state and local spending, and sits on the CalPERS and CalSTRS pension boards. 4-year term.

ca-insurance.learn: Runs the Department of Insurance: approves or rejects home, auto and health insurance rate changes and enforces insurance law. 4-year term.

ca-sos.learn: Chief elections officer who certifies ballot measures and results, and keeper of business filings. 4-year term.

ca-spi.learn: Nonpartisan head of the state Department of Education; administers K-12 programs and is executive officer of the State Board of Education. 4-year term.

ca-treasurer.learn: The state's banker: sells state bonds, invests state money, and manages state cash. 4-year term.

ca-gov.learn: Signs or vetoes bills (with line-item veto on spending), proposes the state budget each January, appoints judges and agency heads, and can grant pardons. 4-year term.

ca-ltgov.learn: Acting governor when the governor is absent, President of the State Senate with a tie-breaking vote, and member of UC Regents and CSU Trustees. 4-year term.

ca-boe-2.learn: One of five members (four elected plus the Controller) overseeing property tax assessment, the alcoholic beverage tax and the tax on insurers. 4-year term.

sf-assessor-recorder.learn: Determines which San Francisco properties are subject to property tax and assesses their value. 4-year term; current salary $267,488.

sf-public-defender.learn: Provides legal representation to San Franciscans charged with crimes who cannot afford an attorney. 4-year term; current salary $307,892.

sf-supervisor-d6.office: San Francisco Board of Supervisors District 6
sf-supervisor-d6.learn: One of 11 members of the city's legislative branch, which enacts local laws and adopts the annual budget. 4-year term; current salary $180,102.

sf-board-of-education.learn: Seven-member board governing the San Francisco Unified School District (K-12). 4-year terms; $6,000 annual stipend; three seats on this ballot.

sf-community-college-board.learn: Seven-member board governing City College and other adult learning centers. 4-year terms; $6,000 stipend; three full-term seats plus one unexpired term on this ballot.

austin-isd-trustees.office: Austin ISD Board of Trustees (Districts 1, 4, 6, 7 and At-Large 9)
austin-isd-trustees.learn: Nine-member elected board that sets the direction of Austin ISD educational programs and services. 4-year terms, filled on a rotating basis.

tx-sboe-5.office: Texas State Board of Education District 5

travis-commissioner.office: Travis County Commissioner (precinct for 78701 to verify)

travis-jp.office: Travis County Justice of the Peace (precinct for 78701 to verify)

tcad-board.office: Travis Central Appraisal District Board, Places 1-3

ca-court-of-appeal-retention.office: California Court of Appeal, First District Justices (retention)
